title: Predicting critical temperature in quantum simulators for high-$T_c$ superconductivity: the matrix product state plus mean field approach
abstract: Quantum simulation based on ultra cold atomic lattice gases is one of the most promising platforms to investigate high-$T_c$ superconductivity beyond the limited capabilities of quantum many body numerics on classical computers. Yet, despite enormous progress since the field's inception, realizing a high-$T_c$ superconducting state still remains out of reach. The present work lays the groundwork to purpose the recently proposed, and already partly realized, mixed-dimensional (mixD) models, towards this end. These systems offer the proven capability to realize very high pairing energies while retaining appreciable mobility of pairs. We specifically investigate the potential of 2D mixD-models with anisotropic tunneling, using the matrix product state plus mean field theory (MPS+MF) for fermions, and show that these models may enter a high-$T_c$ superconducting phase. These simulations in turn are based on a comprehensive characterization of the 1D mixD-systems, which are the sub-units of which the 2D system is comprized. In this, we cover the range of currently experimentally relevant system sizes, and establish practical heuristics to determine when finite\hyp size effects preclude the use of a 1D mixD-system to build the 2D ones.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework using the Matrix Product State plus Mean Field approach to study high-Tc superconductivity in mixed-dimensional (mixD) lattice models. By treating the system as coupled 1D ladders, the authors predict that these structures can realize a high-Tc superconducting state. This work is significant because it provides a detailed, numerically grounded method to analyze complex correlated electron physics relevant to next-generation quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to predict the critical temperature (Tc) for high-Tc superconductivity, moving beyond the limitations of the standard 2D Hubbard model.
main_result: The study predicts that 2D mixed-dimensional (mixD) models, when simulated using the MPS+MF approach, can enter a high-Tc superconducting phase, contrary to some previous expectations regarding pairing energy.
method: The core method is the Matrix Product State plus Mean Field (MPS+MF) theory applied to characterize coupled 1D ladder systems, which are then assembled into 2D bilayer models.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by mixed-dimensional (mixD) lattices, specifically 2D bilayers composed of coupled 1D ladders, governed by a t-J type Hamiltonian. This is investigated in the context of quantum simulation using ultra-cold atomic lattice gases.
key_observables: Pairing energy (Ep), spin gap (Es), superconducting stiffness (rho_c), and the critical temperature (Tc).
important_parameters: Anisotropic tunneling parameters, system size (limited to experimentally relevant sizes), and the ratio function R(Kc).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the MPS+MF approximation, which is assumed valid when inter-ladder coupling is smaller than the pairing and spin gaps; the results are also limited by achievable finite system sizes.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) shows the 2D mixD model structure, and Figure 8 illustrates the ratio function R(Kc) as a function of the Luttinger parameter Kc.
paper_structure: The work first characterizes 1D mixD systems using MPS+MF, establishing heuristics for their use as building blocks. It then extends this to 2D bilayer systems, calculating key superconducting diagnostics (Ep, Es, Tc) based on the effective Hamiltonian derived via mean-field theory.
why_interesting: The combination of MPS+MF theory with the physical context of cold atom quantum simulation for high-Tc superconductivity provides a concrete, computationally tractable pathway to study complex strongly correlated physics.
